item.title: The Start Time of Ringdown
item.description: arXiv:2611.05472v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We determine the convergence of quasi-normal modes sums for a point-particle plunging into a Schwarzschild black hole. While a dynamical amplitude model reproduces the waveform after the particle crosses the bounce radius, a constant amplitude sum converges only after the start time $t_S$, which corresponds to the advanced time at which the particle hits the central singularity. For a plunge from the ISCO, $t_S \simeq 9.4 M$ after the peak of the $22$ mode. After $t_S$, dynamical and constant amplitudes models are equivalent; our analysis also implies that any "direct wave" must reduce to the late-time tail after $t_S$.
item.dc:creator: Adrien Kuntz

item.title: The quasi-topological space of quasi-topological gravities
item.description: arXiv:2611.05485v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate general properties of quasi-topological theories of gravity involving infinite towers of polynomial densities and of their regular vacuum black hole solutions. We show that every positive-mass regular vacuum solution necessarily possesses a de Sitter core, while Minkowski and anti-de Sitter cores are excluded. Regarding the horizon structure, we prove that asymptotically flat and anti-de Sitter regular black holes always admit extremal configurations. We find that there is no upper bound on the number of horizons and that horizons of arbitrarily high degeneracy can arise. These results extend to more general theories of gravity with second-order equations on spherically symmetric backgrounds. Finally, we characterize the space of quasi-topological theories admitting regular black holes, showing that it is contractible (in particular, path-connected and simply connected) and that regularity is stable under suitably small deformations of the higher-order couplings. In the sense of Spanier, this space is naturally a contractible \emph{quasi-topological} space. Additionally, we prove that any theory defined by a set of couplings up to any arbitrarily high, but finite, curvature order can be completed into a theory yielding regular black hole solutions, while preserving the same set of lower-order couplings. These results show that regular solutions arise in a broad class of quasi-topological gravities and do not require fine-tuning of the couplings.
item.dc:creator: Pablo Bueno, Robie A. Hennigar, Matteo G. Marrone, \'Angel J. Murcia

item.title: Black hole quasinormal mode excitation and mixing for coupled fields
item.description: arXiv:2611.05488v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The idea of testing the nature of black holes and possible deviations from general relativity from their oscillation spectrum, known as ``black hole spectroscopy'', has become an experimental science. In many modified theories of gravity, the gravitational perturbations couple to additional degrees of freedom, leading to mode mixing and to a more complex ringdown signal. We adopt the parametrized quasinormal mode formalism for nonrotating black holes to study coupled perturbations in modified gravity theories in order to understand how the interaction with additional fields affects the quasinormal mode frequencies and their amplitudes. We compute the quasinormal mode spectrum of the coupled system in the frequency domain using direct integration and a matrix-valued continued-fraction method. We then compare the results with time-domain evolutions, where we extract the mode frequencies and amplitudes using the Prony method as well as least-squares fitting. In the weak-coupling regime, the scaling of the amplitudes associated with the gravitational-led and secondary-led modes can be understood perturbatively. The excitation of additional families of ringdown modes can become significant even when the frequency shifts remain moderate. We use our numerical time evolutions to provide ready-to-use coefficients for the mode amplitudes for representative initial data configurations. We work out specific examples, including dynamical Chern-Simons gravity and the special near-resonant case of coupled perturbations between the polar and axial quasinormal modes. Our theory-agnostic characterization of coupled systems should be useful to quantify systematic effects in black hole spectroscopy with next-generation gravitational-wave detectors.
item.dc:creator: Caio F. B. Macedo, Orival R. de Medeiros, Emanuele Berti, Hector O. Silva, Sebastian H. V\"olkel

item.title: Geodesic completeness and photon propagation in a superconducting T-duality black hole
item.description: arXiv:2611.05630v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The purpose of this article is twofold. First, we study the geodesic completeness of the string T-duality black hole with the Raychaudhuri equation, for radial massive particles of arbitrary specific energy $\varepsilon$. Exact proper-time quadratures reveal three classes of observers: supercritical observers reach the regular centre in finite proper time through a caustic and pass through it, critical observers ($\varepsilon=1$) approach it only asymptotically with finite expansion, and subcritical observers are reflected at a fold caustic. Because the lapse is analytic and even in $r$, geodesics continue regularly through the centre, and all three classes are complete on the stipulated maximal extension. A diverging expansion therefore signals a caustic of the congruence rather than an endpoint of the geodesics, in contrast with Schwarzschild spacetime. Second, radial Maxwell rays are likewise complete but form a single class, since a massless ray carries no energy scale. We propose to model the black-hole core itself as a superconductor, with London response $\mu^2=4\pi\kappa\rho$ attributed to the existing source. A symmetry-breaking potential with a vacuum-energy offset reproduces the de Sitter core and its photon mass exactly at the centre and approximately in the inner core; since no static scalar theory reproduces the anisotropic source further out, the full radial response remains phenomenological. The resulting Hamiltonian rays follow timelike geodesics of $\mu^2g_{\mu\nu}$ up to reparametrisation and reproduce the three classes, separated by the central mass $\mu_0$, while the density gradient of the core adds a defocusing contribution near the centre. We also distinguish Hamiltonian completeness from completeness of the conformal metric.
item.dc:creator: Kimet Jusufi

item.title: Bumblebee radiation from neutral matter around a black hole
item.description: arXiv:2611.05676v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate bumblebee radiation generated by neutral matter orbiting a black hole with a radial spacelike vector vacuum. Starting from a point particle coupled minimally to the metric, we derive the curvature induced vector current and the potential response required by its conservation. For a localized circular source with no independent radial boundary current, this response gives $\delta V'=\xi\rho/4$. The axial vector source instead follows the radial transport of angular momentum and vanishes for circular motion. A slightly eccentric orbit excites an axial dipole at the orbital frequency $\Omega$ and a quadrupole contribution at $2\Omega$, with outgoing amplitudes proportional to $ev^3$ and $ev^4$, respectively, where $v=\sqrt{M/a}$. We construct their retarded response and obtain the leading coefficients through weak field matching. Reconstruction of the observer's tidal tensor gives the dipole strain $h_{\hat r\hat\phi}^{V,10}=\xi^2b^2\mu ev^3\sin\theta\cos[\Omega(t-R)]/(8\pi R)$. The corresponding partial luminosity is $P_{B,10}^{\infty}=\xi^2b^2\mu^2e^2v^{12}/(48\pi M^2)$ at the leading order. Remarkably, the ordinary neutral matter produces an additional radial transverse tidal signal even when the homogeneous gravitational master operator remains in Schwarzschild form.
item.dc:creator: A. A. Ara\'{u}jo Filho

item.title: Exact teleportation bounds for fermionic Hawking thermality beyond the single-mode approximation
item.description: arXiv:2611.05773v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fermionic teleportation near a Schwarzschild horizon involves two physically distinct ingredients that are often varied together: Hawking thermal mixing and the relative composition of the right and left Unruh modes. We separate them by factorizing the reduced map of the detected exterior fermionic mode into a mode-preparation channel and a Hawking thermal channel. At fixed right-left Unruh-mode composition, we then solve a global constrained quantum-channel optimization over all two-qubit resource states whose fully entangled fraction remains at or below the standard teleportation threshold immediately before thermal mixing. A parity twirl and positivity reduce the arbitrary-state problem exactly to a two-variable quadratic optimization. The solution yields a necessary-and-sufficient activation boundary, a second exact boundary for attaining the universal optimum, and explicit optimizing states. The resulting phase diagram contains a strict no-go region, a composition-limited activation region, and a universal-bound region. The analysis converts state-specific observations of Hawking-assisted teleportation into exact channel-level bounds over the full two-qubit state space.
item.dc:creator: Zhiming Huang

item.title: Spacetime Evolution Induced by a Massive Cosmic String in Numerical Relativity
item.description: arXiv:2611.05996v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cosmic strings are one-dimensional topological defects formed during phase transitions in the early universe. ''Massive'' cosmic strings possess a sufficiently large tension to close their transverse space, forming a conical singularity outside the string, as a static gravitational effect. In a dynamical context, such strings are expected to drive topological inflation. In this work, we investigate the spacetime evolution induced by the formation of a massive cosmic string in a radiation-dominated cosmological background, imposing cylindrical symmetry. Using full numerical relativity simulations, we observe that the string core undergoes topological inflation and that its boundary moves inwards superluminally, which causally disconnects the core from the outer universe. Between the core and the asymptotic regions, a nearly matter-dominated decelerating region originates sourced by the oscillating string fields. This region is bounded by a local maximum (''belly'') and local minimum (''throat'') of the circumferential radius, while the throat recedes outwards at about 10% the speed of light. Furthermore, a gravitational wavefront is emitted from the string, characterizing the light cone of the string formation. Even behind the wavefront, the exterior region no longer exhibits a ''conical'' structure. Based on the simulation results, we construct a Penrose diagram, reflecting the causal structure of the entire spacetime.
item.dc:creator: Yoshihiro Kishimoto, Cristian Joana, Teruaki Suyama

item.title: Research on gravitational waves from extreme mass ratio inspirals in an axisymmetric Finslerian extension of Schwarzschild spacetime
item.description: arXiv:2611.06018v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate gravitational waves from extreme mass ratio inspirals in an axisymmetric Finslerian extension of the Schwarzschild spacetime. Its angular component is described by a two-dimensional Randers space, with the Schwarzschild limit recovered at Finslerian parameter $\epsilon = 0$. This structure breaks spherical symmetry, causing generic orbits to undergo orbital plane precession. Using multipolar radiation reaction and adiabatic orbital averaging, we derive the leading order Finslerian corrections to the energy, axial angular momentum, and total angular momentum fluxes. These corrections enter at Newtonian order and take different forms. We then incorporate these corrections into a higher-order Schwarzschild hybrid flux model to evolve the orbital elements and construct waveforms at mass quadrupole order using the numerical kludge method. The Finslerian corrections affect both the conservative orbital dynamics and the dissipative inspiral, producing cumulative phase shifts relative to the Schwarzschild waveform. For the representative source observed by LISA over one year with signal-to-noise ratio of 20, the noise weighted mismatch analysis shows that Finslerian waveforms with $|\epsilon| \gtrsim 2 \times 10^{-6}$ are distinguishable from their Schwarzschild counterparts, with higher initial eccentricities further lowering the distinguishable value of $|\epsilon|$. For a Schwarzschild injection, the Fisher matrix analysis yields a marginalized $1\sigma$ uncertainty of $\sigma_\epsilon \simeq 1.26 \times 10^{-6}$. These results show the potential of space-based gravitational wave detectors to probe the axisymmetric Finslerian extension of the Schwarzschild spacetime.
item.dc:creator: Jin-Tao Yao, Zhi-Chao Zhao, Xin Li

item.title: Topology change and the Gauss Bonnet term in causal set theory: the sign of the cosmological term and the axion decay constant
item.description: arXiv:2611.06102v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Causal set theory permits changes of spatial topology without the metric degeneracy that forbids them in continuum Lorentzian gravity. In four dimensions such changes enter the gravitational action only through the Gauss--Bonnet term, which is the Euler density. We show that the Euler density of a discrete space is exact, local and combinatorial: it sums to the Euler characteristic at any resolution and is supported on topological defects. The Gauss--Bonnet term of a causal set is therefore fixed rather than postulated. Because it is linear in the number of elements, which is the four-volume, it acts as a cosmological constant. Its coefficient follows without forming any functional derivative, so the known obstruction in the continuum does not arise. The everpresent cosmological constant of causal set theory assumes that the mean topological charge vanishes. We show that it does not. The species of opposite sign solves the field equations only if a positive cosmological constant is already present, and, being simply connected, it cannot carry the axion charge that supports the other species. Only one sign survives, and the sign of the cosmological term is derived rather than assumed. We recover the surviving transition from the causal order alone in every simulated sprinkling. The action of the corresponding axion wormhole then fixes the magnitude. The observed value requires an axion decay constant near the grand unification scale, and this result is insensitive to the one-loop prefactor and to the Gauss--Bonnet coupling.
item.dc:creator: Stylianos A. Tsilioukas

item.title: Coupled membrane response and horizon dissipation in four-dimensional Einstein-scalar-Gauss-Bonnet gravity
item.description: arXiv:2611.06198v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop an action-based membrane paradigm for nonextremal, static, spherically symmetric black holes in four-dimensional Einstein-scalar-Gauss-Bonnet (EsGB) gravity, describing their interaction with external perturbations through an effective fluid membrane. We calculate the linear membrane responses to perturbations and use them to analyze the work done on the membrane and the energy absorbed by the horizon. Horizon energy absorption receives contributions from geometric shear and scalar interactions. The scalar contribution includes both direct work on the membrane and work associated with the induced horizon expansion. We then establish a balance relation between the integrated horizon absorption and the second-order change in Wald entropy between stationary horizon cuts. Applying this framework to slow dynamics near a simple turning point, we obtain the leading exponential growth or decay rate of spherically symmetric scalar perturbations without fitting a dynamical damping coefficient.
item.dc:creator: Yan-Heng Jin, Wen-Biao Han

item.title: Missing solutions in scalar-Gauss-Bonnet gravity
item.description: arXiv:2611.06246v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We discover novel neutron star solutions under scalar-Gauss-Bonnet (sGB) gravity which have been missed altogether in the existing literature. The complete solution space also reveals a new regularity condition that has to be satisfied by all scalarized stars. Certain scalarized branches of neutron star solutions under sGB gravity have long been known to abruptly terminate on stellar mass-radius diagrams at lower stellar radii, a phenomenon that has no counterpart in classical scalar-tensor theories. Such termination has been strongly suspected to be physical rather than a numerical artifact nevertheless, since sGB theories feature a regularity condition at the center of the star, which can prevent the existence of certain configurations. Motivated by the recently re-emerging phase-transition view of scalarization, we first predict that these terminated branches can reappear after a "gap." We confirm this by finding such reappearing branches, and also determine which parts of the theory parameter space are more amenable to such occurrences. We then show that the previously known central regularity condition cannot explain all the non-existing solutions in the gaps, which leads us to the discovery of a new, non-central, condition for the existence of scalarized neutron stars under sGB gravity.
item.dc:creator: O\u{g}uzhan K. Yamak, Kalin V. Staykov, Fethi M. Ramazano\u{g}lu, Daniela D. Doneva, Stoytcho S. Yazadjiev

item.title: Metric reconstruction in a Bondi-like gauge
item.description: arXiv:2611.06367v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Metric perturbations obtained from a Hertz potential in an ingoing radiation gauge (IRG) generically grow in an outgoing coordinate $r$ at future null infinity, and are therefore not asymptotically flat in the Bondi sense. Hollands and Toomani showed that this growth can be removed, within the Green--Hollands--Zimmerman (GHZ) framework, by an IRG-compatible ``residual'' gauge transformation together with a carefully chosen choice of the undetermined integration ``constants'' of the Hertz potential. In this work we turn that proof into a practical algorithm. We show that this entire completion is generated by a single ``Held Master Scalar'' (HMS), which can be thought of as a function on future null infinity. The HMS is obtained from the leading asymptotic piece of the $0$-Weyl scalar through a Teukolsky--Starobinsky inversion. We give explicit formulas for the four integration constants of the Hertz potential associated with the $0$-Weyl scalar, and for the residual gauge vector in terms of the HMS, thereby bringing the metric perturbation into a Bondi-like gauge. In Schwarzschild the entire construction is diagonal in $(\ell, m)$-modes and every completion field is available in closed form; in Kerr the construction is tri-diagonal. We have numerically implemented the full scheme in $(\ell,m)$ and in $m$-modes, including the corrector piece of the GHZ framework. We illustrate our scheme numerically for a point-particle on a circular orbit in a puncture scheme in Schwarzschild and in Kerr, by demonstrating the Bondi-like fall-off. We also find agreement with the known Detweiler redshift computations in Schwarzschild and Kerr. Our method directly gives the Bondi news, mass-, and angular momentum aspects, for which we give exemplary results in Kerr.
item.dc:creator: Marc Casals, Stefan Hollands, Vahid Toomani, Peter Zimmerman

item.title: Constraining Lorentz Invariance Violation via Precision Atomic Spectroscopy
item.description: arXiv:2611.06392v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates Lorentz violation arising from quantum gravity effects in electronic and muonic hydrogen atoms. The violation is modeled through a modified dispersion relation parameterized by a dimensionless coefficient $\xi$ and suppressed by the Planck scale. Using high-precision spectroscopic data and a chi-squared fitting procedure that carefully accounts for theoretical uncertainties in the Rydberg constant and the proton radius, the analysis yields a 95% confidence level constraint $\xi \in [-14.3,\; 1.37] \times 10^5$. The mass scaling of the effect reveals two distinct regimes: for the lowest-order deformation, the heavy nucleus amplifies the signal, while for higher-order corrections, the lepton dominates the sensitivity. These bounds approach Planck-scale sensitivity using the simplest atomic systems, thereby circumventing ambiguities inherent in more complex quantum systems.
item.dc:creator: A. S. Lemos, J. E. J. Matias, F. Dahia, I. P. Lobo

item.title: A Geometric No-Go Theorem for Regular Black Holes in Scalar-Tensor Theories
item.description: arXiv:2611.06460v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Perturbative instabilities generically puzzles singularity-free spacetimes, including non-singular bounce, traversible wormholes and regular black holes (RBHs). Can the scalar-tensor (ST) theories that stabilize the first two also stabilize RBHs? We show that the answer is no for static, spherically symmetric RBHs supported by a radial scalar field within a broad class of ST theories. In any RBHs with two-horizon structure, the ratio of the longitudinal scale to the sphere radius must attain an interior maximum. The proper-time derivative of that ratio is associated to the squared propagation speed of odd-parity tensor perturbations by the background field equations in a broad class of scalar-tensor theories. A Lorentzian odd-tensor cone then requires a local minimum instead of a maximum. This conflicts indicate a geometric no-go theorem, covering a broad class of ST theories including spatially covariant gravity, Horndeski theory, quadratic GLPV, DHOST, and U-DHOST theories, and their admissible disformal extensions. Viable RBHs therefore require relaxing at least one geometric or dynamical assumption.
item.dc:creator: Shulang Peng, Jun Tao, Mian Zhu, Yi-Fu Cai

item.title: Quasinormal modes of charged de Sitter black holes and strong cosmic censorship in conformal Killing gravity
item.description: arXiv:2611.06510v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The strong cosmic censorship conjecture argues that the future evolution of the spacetime should be predictable from the initial data. However, within the framework of general relativity, some counterexamples to the conjecture have been found, especially for de Sitter spacetime. Spurred by challenges to the validity of the strong cosmic censorship conjecture, we extend such investigations to conformal Killing gravity, a promising candidate beyond Einstein's theory. Considering neutral massless scalar perturbations for charged de Sitter black hole, we not only shed light on the quasinormal mode spectrum, but also clarify whether the modifications from conformal Killing gravity and nonlinear electrodynamics can rescue the strong cosmic censorship conjecture, and further investigate how characteristic parameters affect its validity. As the first instance for investigating the conjecture in the framework of conformal Killing gravity, this paper reports some unexpected findings.
item.dc:creator: Gao-Ming Deng, Zong-Yao Zhang, Yiwen Liu, Si-Yuan Pan

item.title: Probing black bounce spacetime through mass accretion rate
item.description: arXiv:2611.06527v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study steady, spherically symmetric accretion of a collisionless kinetic gas onto a compact object described by the Simpson--Visser (SV) metric, a one-parameter regularization of the Schwarzschild spacetime. Using the standard relativistic Vlasov formalism, we adopt boundary conditions at a finite injection radius $R$ and compute the mass accretion rate $\dot{M}$ for Vlasov gas with both monoenergetic and Maxwell--J\"uttner distribution functions. Throughout the computation, we also take into account the influence of particle's angular momentum. We carefully investigate the influence of the black bounce parameter on the mass accretion rate $\dot{M}$. By expanding accretion rate in terms of bounce parameter $a$, we found that the leading-order correction appears at quadratic order in $a$. This work extends the Vlasov accretion framework to a broader class of spherically symmetric spacetimes and quantifies the impact of the geometric modification on the accretion flow. In particular, since the shadows of the SV and Schwarzschild black holes are degenerate, comparing their mass accretion rates may offer a complementary probe for distinguishing these geometries in future astrophysical observations.
item.dc:creator: Xi-Rui Guo, Ya-Peng Hu, Yu-Sen An

item.title: Dipolar boson stars as static two-body systems: an effective-one-body description
item.description: arXiv:2611.06531v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Dipolar boson stars consist of two scalar-field lumps held in static equilibrium by the balance between gravitational attraction and scalar repulsion. The repulsion stems from a $\pi$ phase difference between the harmonically varying complex scalar field sourcing each lump. We construct sequences of these configurations numerically and describe them analytically as bound states of two boson stars within the effective-one-body (EOB) formalism. We map the EOB potential previously derived for the scattering of two boson stars onto an energy-dependent Schwarzschild-like radial potential. We find that the EOB-based analytical prediction for the binding energy of the system agrees remarkably well with the numerical values. The analytical prediction for the critical gravitational coupling beyond which no static equilibrium exists is also consistent with the numerical results.
item.dc:creator: Thibault Damour, Romain Gervalle, Tamanna Jain

item.title: Quasi-equilibrium tidal folds of white dwarfs around rotating black holes in shift-symmetric Einstein--scalar--Gauss--Bonnet gravity
item.description: arXiv:2611.06647v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We examine how the geometry of rotating black holes in linear, shift-symmetric Einstein--scalar--Gauss--Bonnet (EsGB) gravity changes the limiting tidal equilibria of white dwarfs (WDs). The relativistic tidal field is obtained from numerical EsGB backgrounds in a parallel-transported frame and coupled to a compressible affine model. Comparisons with Kerr black holes matched in Arnowitt--Deser--Misner (ADM) mass and angular momentum show a positive shift in the orbital frequency at the tidal fold. At fixed spin the relative correction follows an approximately quadratic dependence on the EsGB coupling, consistent with the leading response of the metric to the scalar field. Over the sampled backgrounds, the relative correction reaches order $10^{-3}$. Black hole rotation also changes the relation between the tidal fold and the innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO): the sampled prograde folds remain outside the ISCO, while retrograde folds move inside it at higher spins. Orbital orientation therefore controls whether tidal equilibrium is lost before the orbital stability limit is reached. For the stellar and black hole masses considered here, the characteristic gravitational wave (GW) frequencies fall in the millihertz band relevant to planned space based interferometers. Future GW observations capable of resolving deviations from Kerr predictions could constrain the EsGB coupling.
item.dc:creator: Shoupan Liu, Meilin Liu, Yu Wang, Yunqi Liu

item.title: Born-Infeld black holes in bumblebee gravity
item.description: arXiv:2611.06659v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct exact static and spherically symmetric charged solutions in bumblebee gravity minimally coupled to Born--Infeld electrodynamics, taking into account a spacelike vector norm and a vanishing cosmological constant. An independently varied Lagrange multiplier enforces the norm constraint and acquires a radial profile determined by the transverse electromagnetic pressure. The solutions include purely radial configurations and configurations with constant or varying temporal amplitudes. At $\xi=\kappa/2$, the varying temporal amplitude introduces an independent bumblebee field strength while preserving the metric of the constant temporal configuration. Moreover, the electric field remains bounded, and the temporal configurations admit smooth extensions across a simple future horizon under explicit regularity conditions. We derive the photon sphere and shadow radii for both metric and nonlinear electromagnetic propagation. The leading nonlinear corrections enlarge the shadow at fixed geometric charge, whereas the temporal amplitude enters through the charged lapse. Comparisons with observations of Sgr~A$^*$ and M87$^*$ provide conditional bounds on the charge and nonlinear scale. In addition, the adopted planetary perihelion allowances yield an illustrative sensitivity of $|\xi|(b^2+u_0^2)\lesssim2.6\times10^{-12}$ for a neutral solar exterior.
item.dc:creator: A. A. Ara\'{u}jo Filho, E. M. Siquieri, N. Heidari, V. B. Bezerra, A. F. Santos

item.title: Inflationary attractors in metric-affine gravity
item.description: arXiv:2611.06750v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study single-field slow-roll inflation in metric-affine gravity (MAG). We consider the most general action up to operators linear in curvature and quadratic in the distortion, without propagating torsion and non-metricity. We first impose projective invariance and promote every coefficient to a function of the scalar field. After integrating out the non-dynamical distortion, the net contribution is a correction $k(\phi)$ to the scalar kinetic term. We then consider the class of $\xi$-attractors for which the non-minimal couplings and the scalar potential are fixed by a single function $f(\phi)$. It is well-known that in the metric formulation the strong-coupling regime is universally the Starobinsky attractor. In the Palatini framework, instead, this attractor is lost and the predictions become model-dependent. Here, we show that the MAG framework restores universality: in the strong coupling limit with finite ratios of the distortion couplings to $\xi$ we have an $\alpha$-attractor, $n_s=1-2/N_*$ and $r=12\alpha/N_*^2$, with $\alpha=1+\zeta/(6\xi)$. The ratio $\zeta/\xi$ encodes the distortion contribution. Starobinsky and Palatini inflation are recovered as specific limits. Through a numerical parameter scan we show that almost all the healthy points lie on one of the two attractors : either Nieh-Yan-like inflation (studied in a previous work and extended here) or the new MAG $\alpha$-attractor found here. Finally, we explicitly drop projective invariance and analyse the general MAG theory. The same large-field asymptotic structure survives. We conclude that no extra inflationary phenomenology is reached by the non-projectively invariant operators: the $\alpha$-attractor is a general prediction of MAG.
item.dc:creator: Ilaria Andrei, Christian Dioguardi

item.title: Axial black hole perturbations in purely-metric Horndeski theories
item.description: arXiv:2611.06875v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study axial (odd-parity) perturbations about static and spherically-symmetric curvaturised black hole solutions of purely-metric Horndeski theories. We first review the construction of purely-metric theories of gravity with second-order equations of motion and an additional propagating scalar degree of freedom which is purely gravitational. We then revisit the formation, in a subclass of these theories, of a new branch of hairy black hole solutions under tachyonic instabilities of the scalar field near the Schwarzschild solution. Because a non-zero Ricci curvature grows and by analogy with black hole scalarisation, the latter black hole formation mechanism is dubbed \emph{curvaturisation}. We then apply the first-order approach to the dynamics of axial perturbations and find that it is equivalent to that of axial perturbations in general relativity evolving in a distinct effective metric. We explicitly provide that effective metric in terms of the background and the Lagrangian functions, and show that it shares the same causality structure as the background metric of curvaturised black holes. By turning to the Schr\"odinger-like formulation of the perturbations, we analyse the scattering potential and conclude that the axial perturbations of curvaturised black holes are linearly stable. Finally, we confirm these findings by explicitly computing the fundamental quasi-normal mode as well as the first five overtones for the quadrupole $\ell = 2$.
item.dc:creator: H\'elo\"ise Delaporte, Hugo Roussille

item.title: Gravitational-Wave Constraints on $R^2$ Gravity
item.description: arXiv:2611.06902v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Gravitational waves from compact binary coalescences provide a unique opportunity to test general relativity in the strong-field regime. Quadratic $f(R)=R+aR^2$ gravity is among the simplest higher-curvature extensions of general relativity and introduces a massive scalar degree of freedom whose finite interaction range can modify compact-binary dynamics and gravitational-wave emission. We map this theory onto the effective-field-theory waveform for generic massive scalar-tensor gravity, obtaining a theory-specific inspiral phase correction governed by the single coupling parameter $a$. Using Bayesian analyses of the binary-neutron-star events GW170817 and GW190425, we obtain a combined constraint on the quadratic-curvature coupling of $a\lesssim6.2\times10^6\,\mathrm{m}^2$ at $90\%$ credibility, corresponding to a lower bound on the scalar mass of $m_s\gtrsim3.2\times10^{-11}\,\mathrm{eV}$. This constitutes the strongest astrophysical constraint on the quadratic-curvature coupling, improving the previous best bound by approximately five orders of magnitude and demonstrating the sensitivity of binary-neutron-star inspirals to finite-range scalar interactions in the strong-field regime.
item.dc:creator: Pawan Kumar Gupta, Laura Sagunski

item.title: Resonant electroweak clouds around Schwarzschild black holes
item.description: arXiv:2611.03809v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct nonlinear electroweak clouds around Schwarzschild black holes in the bosonic Weinberg-Salam theory. These configurations are supported by harmonically time-dependent charged gauge fields, while their energy-momentum tensor remains static. Regularity at the horizon imposes a resonance condition relating the field frequency to the horizon electrostatic potential. Unlike linear clouds, these solutions exhibit a finite mass and electric charge gap, and exist only up to a maximal horizon size. We obtain both magnetic and electric clouds, including spherically symmetric and dipolar configurations, which reduce to electroweak balls in the vanishing-horizon limit. We also report a new family of dipolar electroweak balls, which can be energetically favoured over their spherical counterparts at fixed electric charge. Our results, obtained in the probe limit for electroweak couplings away from their measured values, establish a new realization of nonlinear resonant vector hair in a non-Abelian gauge-Higgs theory.
item.dc:creator: Carlos Herdeiro, Eugen Radu

item.title: Raychaudhuri-Ehlers Kinematics on Quantum State-Space: Caustics and Extrinsic Quantum Geometry
item.description: arXiv:2611.05499v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quantum mechanics is inherently geometric in that the pure states form a curved complex manifold and the Schr\"odinger evolution defines a Hamiltonian flow on this space. Geometry identifies constraints on flows on quantum state-space that hold independently of their microscopic realization. We uncover such universal behavior in families of geodesic paths on the quantum state-space using the Raychaudhuri-Ehlers equations. We show that the complex structure leads to tidal anisotropy in the curvature, and for Hilbert space dimension $N\geq3$, complete point-emitted geodesic bundles necessarily develop shear and undergo direction-selective focusing at finite distance. We give these geometric results an information-theoretic interpretation in terms of fidelity susceptibility and quantum Fisher information. For ground-state manifolds constrained by physical parameters, we resolve the tidal curvature into Berry-curvature-dependent ambient tides and contributions from extrinsic bending within the full ambient state space. We further relate extrinsic bending to variations in the unitary generator of motion along intrinsic geodesics. We present exact many-body geometric results for the transverse-field XY spin chain. The product structure of the ground state leads to an exact cancellation of the ambient tide, including its Berry-curvature enhancement, by extrinsic curvature contributions. At the zero-field Ising point, we obtain exact results at finite size and show that the shear source for anisotropy-directed motion is entirely extrinsic relative to the full many-body state-space. For the metric in the thermodynamic limit, the geodesic families exhibit repeated $A_2$ fold catastrophes inside the ferromagnetic phase. Our framework thus separates universal state-space effects from those of physical restrictions and exposes their consequences in a paradigmatic many-body system.
item.dc:creator: Neellohit Karmakar, Suraj S. Hegde, Aryan Bhatia

item.title: An obstruction to cosmic acceleration from shift-symmetric dark sector interactions
item.description: arXiv:2611.05560v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Using the effective field theory of cosmological media, we show that derivative interactions in the dark sector between a perfect fluid and a superfluid cannot support slow-roll expansion while remaining free from instabilities. Furthermore, decomposing the dark sector medium into effective dark matter and dark energy components, we find that the stability conditions exclude a phantom-to-non-phantom crossing. Our approach gives a clear route for constructing theoretically viable dark sector models, and highlights the fundamental constraints that stability requirements impose on their cosmological dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Jose Beltr\'{a}n Jim\'{e}nez, Luis J. Garay, Erik Jensko, Mar\'{i}a P\'{e}rez Garrote

item.title: Complex phase diagram and thermodynamic supercriticality of five-dimensional four-charge AdS black holes in $STU-W^2U$ gauged supergravity
item.description: arXiv:2611.05624v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we investigate the complex phase structure and thermodynamic supercriticality of static four-charge anti-de Sitter (AdS) black holes in five-dimensional $STU-W^2U$ gauged supergravity, with all four physical electric charges held fixed. A Van der Waals-like first-order small/large black hole phase transition is found to terminate at a critical point. By analytically continuing the fixed-charge thermodynamic relations, we trace the two real spinodal singularities through criticality into a complex-conjugate pair in the supercritical region. The corresponding spinodal temperatures exhibit the characteristic $3/2$ near-critical scaling, connecting the subcritical temperature splitting with the imaginary parts of the supercritical complex temperatures. We construct the associated complex phase diagram and identify a Widom-type crossover line from the real-temperature projection of the complex spinodals. This line progressively deviates from the locus of real heat-capacity maxima as the pressure increases. At higher pressures, the real heat-capacity extrema eventually merge and disappear, while the complex spinodal singularities persist. Together, these results reveal a continuous connection between critical phase transitions and supercritical thermodynamics through complex singularity structures, providing further insight into the thermodynamic phase behavior of multicharge supergravity black holes.
item.dc:creator: Di Wu, Xiao-Dan Zhu

item.title: Observational Test of the Maximum-Entropy Conjecture for Black-Hole Mergers with GW250114
item.description: arXiv:2611.05718v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The remnants of binary black-hole (BBH) mergers are accurately described by numerical relativity, but the physical principle governing the selection of the final states remains unclear. A recently proposed maximum-entropy conjecture suggests that a BBH merger produces the Kerr BH that maximizes the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy, subject to the post-Newtonian formalism or balance laws for energy and angular momentum. In this work, we test this conjecture with the event GW250114, inferring the progenitor and remnant properties from the observed pre-merge and post-merge signals, separately. We construct the surrogate Kerr entropy associated with candidate remnant states along the inferred energy-angular-momentum trajectory. We then compare the maximum-entropy state with the independently inferred mass and dimensionless spin of the final BH. We find that the conjecture predicts a remnant mass of $M_f=70.0^{+0.35}_{-0.21}\,M_\odot$ and spin of $\chi_f=0.70^{+0.00}_{-0.01}$, compared with the ringdown estimates $M_f={72.3}^{+3.6}_{-3.7}\,M_\odot$ and $\chi_f=0.74^{+0.05}_{-0.07}$. The entropy deviation is consistent with zero within the $68\%$ credible interval for our fiducial analysis, and variations in the pre-merger truncation time and quasi-normal modes (QNM) content reveal no compelling discrepancy with the conjecture.
item.dc:creator: Yang Jiang, Qing-Guo Huang

item.title: The Cosmology of Hawking Axions
item.description: arXiv:2611.05747v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Since primordial black holes (PBH) are always non-relativistic, their cosmological energy fraction grows relative to that of radiation. Thus, for even a tiny initial PBH abundance, the universe generically enters an epoch of early matter domination, which ends when the PBH evaporate to restore the hot big bang. We consider the possibility that a PBH dominated era yields a population of boosted axion-like particles (ALPs) produced from Hawking evaporation. Eventually these ``Hawking axions" become non-relativistic and decay to photons, which can affect various cosmological and astrophysical observables. Here we place new constraints on these particles through their impact on big bang nucleosynthesis, cosmic microwave background, large-scale structure, and X-ray observables. Furthermore, if Hawking axions remain relativistic through recombination, then depending on the progenitor PBH mass, they contribute $\Delta N_{\rm eff}\simeq0.05$-$0.11$, which may be observable with future CMB probes.
item.dc:creator: Abdelaziz Hussein, Gordan Krnjaic, Sarunas Verner

item.title: Unsupervised Neural Operators for Rotating Relativistic Stars: High-Fidelity Equation of State Inference and Pulsar Spin Evolution at Scale
item.description: arXiv:2611.05790v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Observed populations of rotating neutron stars~(NSs) with millisecond-order periods are powerful probes of fundamental physics. Mass-radius measurements inform poorly constrained properties of degenerate nuclear matter, whereas high-fidelity population synthesis connects unknowns in NS formation and binary evolution to large radio-timing surveys. However, repeated structure calculations are prohibitive due to the computational cost of solving the highly coupled partial differential equations of axisymmetric general relativistic hydrostatic equilibrium that govern rotating NS interiors. Non-rotating calculations or approximate rotational corrections can bias equation of state inference and limit the fidelity of population synthesis in tracing the evolutionary history of progenitors and propagating equation of state uncertainties. In this \textit{Letter}, we develop physics-informed neural operators that can solve the axisymmetric problem with high accuracy and negligible computational cost. \textit{Our solvers are trained in a fully unsupervised setting, with the training objective informed solely by the partial differential equations, and achieve a $10^3\times$ speed-up with negligible accuracy loss}. These solvers enable scalable EoS inference that self-consistently accounts for rotation and repeated stellar-structure calculations during binary evolution, making spin predictions that account for rotational structure and EoS uncertainties computationally accessible to population synthesis.
item.dc:creator: Anarya Ray

item.title: Gravitational-Wave Microlensing as a Probe of Compact Object Population
item.description: arXiv:2611.05947v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The abundance of compact objects ranging from stellar to intermediate masses ($\sim 1 - 10^{5}M_{\odot}$) remains poorly constrained, particularly for populations such as primordial black holes and dark matter subhalos that emit little or no electromagnetic radiation. Gravitational-wave (GW) microlensing provides a complementary way to probe these populations through wave-optics effects imprinted on the GW signals, with implications for astrophysical and cosmological inference. We develop a hierarchical Bayesian framework to infer the population properties of microlenses from an ensemble of microlensed GW events, constraining the slope of the power-law lens mass function ($\alpha_{\rm ML}$), the lens number density ($n_0$), and the fraction of dark matter in compact lenses ($f_{\rm DM}$). Using simulated microlensed GW signals drawn from a realistic binary black hole population, we find that $\sim 100$ detected microlensed events are able to constrain both $\alpha_{\rm ML}$ and $n_0$, although a degeneracy between the two remains. For a low-mass-dominated lens population ($\alpha_{\rm ML}=2$) with $n_0=10^6~\mathrm{Mpc}^{-3}$, a three-year observation at the O4 sensitivity yields $\sim 130$ detectable microlensed events and recovers the injected dark-matter fraction, $f_{\rm DM}\simeq 1.2 \times 10^{-4}$, with a 90% credible interval of $7.3 \times 10^{-5} \lesssim f_{\rm DM} \lesssim 1.8 \times 10^{-4}$.
item.dc:creator: Eungwang Seo, Jose Mar\'ia Ezquiaga, Martin Hendry

item.title: Non-compact Kogut-Susskind gauge theories: 1D lattice models with exact ${\rm SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ gauge invariance
item.description: arXiv:2611.06771v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Kogut-Susskind (KS) formulation of gauge theories constructs quantum many-body Hamiltonians with gauge invariance under a compact Lie group exactly implemented on a spatial lattice. Here, we revisit this construction for a non-compact gauge group. Although motivated in part by theories like general relativity whose first-order formulation involves the non-compact Lorentz group as a local symmetry, we focus on simpler cases in one spatial dimension akin to the Schwinger model. In a bottom-up approach, we show how exact gauge invariance under the simplest non-compact Lie group ${\rm SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ can be retained exactly on a 1D lattice, and highlight the differences that arise with respect to compact gauge groups, including a continuous spectrum of the Casimir operators of the gauge fields and the emergence of infinite-dimensional representations of the matter fields. For the pure gauge theory, we discuss how a consistent restriction to the positive semigroup ${\rm SL}^{+}(2,\mathbb{R})$ reproduces well-known results from the quantization of Jackiw-Teitelboim (JT) gravity. Motivated by the constraint structure of general dilaton gravity, we introduce static charges coupled to the non-compact gauge field, which can be realised by single-fermion degrees of freedom living in an additional, synthetic dimension. With static charges our lattice model remains exactly integrable, but when extending to dynamical fermionic matter, we arrive at an interacting 1D ${\rm SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ KS gauge theory. We give an interpretation of this model as a chain of charges sequentially connected by strings whose tension pulls matter left or right depending on the sign of the relative continuous ${\rm SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ fluxes. This picture becomes exact when the involved ${\rm SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ charges are strongly self-interacting, where we solve the reduced two-body problem analytically.
item.dc:creator: Carlos Fulgado-Claudio, Torsten V. Zache

item.title: Probing gravity at megahertz frequencies with levitated rotors
item.description: arXiv:2611.06893v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The near-field gravitational interaction between masses is always thought of as instantaneous, an assumption experimentally tested only up to 1.7 kHz, where measurements yield a bounds at the $10^{-5}$ s level. We propose a near-field experiment reaching up to megahertz frequencies, in which a levitated microrotor modulates a mass quadrupole and a second rotor measures the resulting gravitational tidal field as a torque. Because the detector rotor acts as a mechanical local oscillator, the megahertz signal is downconverted to a convenient band of a few hertz, and since at fixed geometry neither the torque nor the integration time depends on the rotation rate, higher frequencies are reached at no cost in sensitivity. With parameters within reach of magnetically levitated NdFeB rotors, a signal at 2 MHz yields a torque of $2\cdot 10^{-25}$ Nm, detectable in under an hour at 10 mK. Treating a possible departure from instantaneous gravitational coupling through a field relaxation time, the measured torque could constrain it at the $10^{-8}$ s level, improving on the existing bounds by more than three orders of magnitude. As a byproduct of our analysis, we derive the sensitivity of a rotor operated as a tunable high-frequency gravitational-wave detector, finding that a noise-equivalent strain around $10^{-22}$ Hz$^{-1/2}$ could be achievable in the megahertz band.
item.dc:creator: Matteo Fadel, Andrea Vinante

item.title: Relativistic Elasticity II
item.description: arXiv:2303.05870v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper is based on a series of talks given at the ESI program on 'Mathematical Perspectives of Gravitation Beyond the Vacuum Regime' in February 2022. It is meant to be an introduction to the field of relativistic elasticity for readers with a good base in the mathematics of General Relativity with no necessary previous of knowledge of elasticity either in the classical or relativistic domain. Despite its introductory purpose, the present work has new material, in particular related to the formal structure of the theory.
item.dc:creator: Robert Beig

item.title: Evolutionary Phase of Universe in $f(R,L_m,T)$ Gravity: The Dynamical System Analysis
item.description: arXiv:2602.08562v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, the dynamical system analysis has been performed to analyze the dynamical behavior of the Universe in $f(R,L_m,T)$ gravity with a scalar field. A well motivated potential function and the linear form of the functional $f(R,L_m,T)$ have been incorporated into the Friedmann equation, and the autonomous dynamical system has been framed by introducing dimensionless variables. The stability behavior of the critical points is obtained and analyzed based on their corresponding eigenvalues. Moreover, cosmological parameters such as the deceleration parameter and the dynamical parameters such as equation of state and density parameters are obtained using the dimensionless variables. It has been observed that the system provides critical points that describe different evolutionary phases of the Universe.
item.dc:creator: R. R. Panchal, Divya G. Sanjava, A. H. Hasmani, B. Mishra

item.title: Direction-of-arrival estimation of a gravitational wave by correlations between quadrupole moments of pulsar timing data
item.description: arXiv:2602.21607v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Can we estimate the direction of arrival (DOA) of a gravitational wave (GW) signal from pulsar timing array observations? The present paper addresses the inverse problem, for which we consider quadrupole moments of pulsar timing data due to GWs from a dominant isolated source such as a binary of supermassive black holes over an isotropic stochastic background. Correlations between the quadrupole moments are discussed as a possible alternative to the matched filtering technique, where the correlations between pulsar pairs over the full sky are taken into account. The correlations turn out to be in the form of a three-dimensional traceless matrix with rank 3 that can be closely related with a projection tensor for the GW. Thereby, we demonstrate that the rank-3 matrix allows to estimate the DOA of the GW without assuming a template bank nor a priori Gaussian noise. A mean over the celestial sphere is adopted instead of the pulsar averaging. A weighted average is used for a non-uniform distribution of pulsars on the sky, for which the Voronoi tessellation is employed to numerically calculate an area-weighted mean. In expectation of the forthcoming Square Kilometre Array, DOA estimation errors are also examined.
item.dc:creator: Taichi Ueyama, Hodaka Tamura, Hideki Asada

item.title: Cosmologically viable non-polynomial quasi-topological gravity: explicit models, $\Lambda$CDM limit and observational constraints
item.description: arXiv:2604.13002v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the cosmological implications of a phenomenologically relevant subclass of non-polynomial quasi-topological gravity (NPQTG), in which the background dynamics is encoded in a single function of the Hubble parameter. This framework provides a minimal and theoretically consistent extension of general relativity, incorporating higher-curvature effects while preserving second-order field equations and avoiding higher-derivative instabilities. We first establish the general conditions for cosmological viability and construct explicit realizations, including polynomial, quartic, power-law and non-polynomial models, demonstrating how different functional forms lead to distinct expansion histories. Focusing on the quartic and power-law cases, we investigate their late-time cosmological evolution, showing that they exhibit a matter-dominated epoch followed by a dark-energy-dominated epoch, and give rise to an effective dark-energy sector of geometric origin, with dynamical equation-of-state behavior that can lie in the quintessence or phantom regime. We then confront the models with observational data from Type Ia Supernovae, Cosmic Chronometers, and Baryon Acoustic Oscillations, using a Bayesian MCMC analysis. We find that both models are fully compatible with the considered data and reproduce the late-time expansion history with a quality of fit comparable to that of $\Lambda$CDM, although the current observations do not provide statistically significant evidence for a departure from the concordance scenario. Our results demonstrate that NPQTG offers a simple and efficient framework for describing late-time cosmic acceleration with dynamical dark energy, while maintaining theoretical consistency and observational viability.
item.dc:creator: Emmanuel N. Saridakis

item.title: Accurate waveforms for generic planar-orbit binary black holes: The multipolar effective-one-body model SEOBNRv6EHM
item.description: arXiv:2605.28715v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Accurate and computationally efficient waveform models are required to infer the parameters of compact binaries from their gravitational wave (GW) emission. Among these parameters, orbital eccentricity serves as a smoking gun for dynamical formation channels and must be accounted for to avoid systematic errors in GW analyses. Here, we present SEOBNRv6EHM, a time-domain, multipolar waveform model for binaries on generic planar orbits, calibrated to quasi-circular (QC) numerical-relativity (NR) simulations from the SXS collaboration. In addition to the dominant $(2,2)$ mode, the model provides the $(2,1)$, $(3,3)$, $(3,2)$, $(4,4)$, and $(4,3)$ multipoles for the full inspiral-merger-ringdown process of coalescing binaries, as well as for dynamical captures and scattering encounters. The model is built within the effective-one-body (EOB) framework, and it employs novel resummations of the radiation-reaction force and waveform modes. We validate its accuracy through comparisons against 592 QC, 319 eccentric, one dynamical-capture, and two scattering SXS NR waveforms, and through scattering-angle comparisons against 61 SXS NR simulations. For QC and small-eccentricity binaries, its accuracy is comparable to previous-generation SEOBNRv5 models. For highly eccentric systems, however, SEOBNRv6EHM attains unprecedented accuracy, with waveform mismatches remaining below or close to $ 2\% $ across the total mass range $ 20-200\, \mathrm{M}_\odot $ for eccentricities up to $\sim 0.9$ at 14 periastron passages before merger. Additionally, SEOBNRv6EHM achieves waveform-generation walltimes that are $ 2 - 8 $ times faster than other state-of-the-art EOB eccentric models, enabling efficient and accurate applications in GW astronomy.
item.dc:creator: Aldo Gamboa, Alessandra Buonanno, Lorenzo Pompili, Raffi Enficiaud, Michael Boyle, Lawrence E. Kidder, Oliver Long, Peter James Nee, Harald P. Pfeiffer, Antoni Ramos-Buades, Mark A. Scheel

item.title: Primordial Black Holes from Vector-Induced Curvature Perturbations Sourced by Primordial Magnetic Fields
item.description: arXiv:2606.23307v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Generating an appreciable abundance of primordial black holes (PBHs) requires a substantial enhancement of primordial curvature perturbations on small scales. In this Letter, we propose a new post-inflationary mechanism in which such an enhancement arises during a stiff, or kination, epoch. The mechanism is driven by metric vector perturbations sourced by the vector component of the electromagnetic stress-energy tensor associated with primordial magnetic fields (PMFs). Since these first-order vector modes remain approximately constant during kination, they act as persistent nonlinear sources for second-order scalar perturbations. We show that the resulting vector-induced curvature perturbations are amplified toward the infrared cutoff of the kination band and exhibit the characteristic scaling $\mathcal P_{\mathcal R}(k)\propto k^{-5}$. As a concrete realization, we consider PMFs generated in a Ratra-type magnetogenesis scenario and find that the induced curvature perturbations can produce PBHs with an abundance large enough to constitute a substantial fraction of the dark matter.
item.dc:creator: Chang Han, Zu-Cheng Chen, Hongwei Yu, Puxun Wu

item.title: Gravitational Wave Birefringence in generalized Palatini Chern Simons
item.description: arXiv:2607.20689v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The cosmological propagation of gravitational waves (GWs) can exhibit amplitude and phase polarization distortions when parity symmetry is broken, a phenomenon known as cosmological birefringence. In this paper, we investigate the phenomenology of GW birefringence in a gravitational model $f(R)$ coupled to a dynamical Chern-Simons (dCS) term, analyzed in the metric and Palatini formalisms. At the background level, this model can lead to dynamical dark energy, while for GW propagation we find that the Palatini formalism predicts both amplitude and velocity birefringence, whereas the metric formalism predicts amplitude birefringence only. We also find that the birefringence effects can either be suppressed or enhanced by the $f(R)$ interactions, depending on the specific form of $f(R)$. Considering three common $f(R)$ models (Hu-Sawicki, Exponential, and Hyperbolic gravity) fit to recent cosmological data, we find that birefringence is enhanced relative to the $f(R) = R$ case, by $1-10\%$ in the Palatini formalism and up to a factor of 2 in the metric formalism. We also translate current GW birefringence constraints to bounds on the dCS coupling within our model. Finally, we show that in our model the birefringence effect grows polynomially with source redshift, in contrast to the linear-distance scaling commonly assumed in phenomenological models of GW birefringence in the current literature.
item.dc:creator: Jose Perdiguero, Macarena Lagos

item.title: Thermodynamic topology of magnetic GMGHS black holes: the $\overline {W}^{1-}$ subclass
item.description: arXiv:2609.20898v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Thermodynamic topology provides a topological classification of black hole states and their branch structures in thermodynamic parameter space. We investigate the thermodynamic topology of the charged nonextremal magnetic Gibbons--Maeda family in four-dimensional asymptotically flat Einstein--Maxwell--dilaton gravity, with particular emphasis on its string-theory member at the dilaton coupling $a=1$, the Gibbons--Maeda--Garfinkle--Horowitz--Strominger (GMGHS) black hole. An analytic classification over the complete domain of regular outer horizons shows that the dilaton coupling separates the family into three limiting structures of the inverse Hawking temperature. At $a=1$, the GMGHS defect curve approaches a nonzero lower inverse temperature endpoint and contains a single unstable branch. In particular, the magnetic GMGHS black hole provides an explicit realization of the previously proposed $\overline W^{1-}$ thermodynamic topological subclass within an asymptotically flat Einstein--Maxwell--dilaton solution. This result demonstrates that the global topological number $W$ alone does not completely characterize black hole thermodynamic topology. The asymptotic behavior of the inverse Hawking temperature near the boundaries of the physical horizon domain provides an additional criterion for distinguishing thermodynamic topological subclasses with the same $W$.
item.dc:creator: Dejiang Yin, Qi-Qi Liang, Yu-Die Wan, Li-Yun Zhang

item.title: Grey-body factors of black holes
item.description: arXiv:2610.24356v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Grey-body factors describe the frequency-dependent transmission of fields through the effective potential generated by a black hole or another compact object. They convert the idealized thermal spectrum of Hawking radiation into the spectrum measured by an observer, determine absorption and scattering cross sections, and provide real-frequency observables complementary to quasinormal modes. In this review, we present a unified account of grey-body factors in black-hole physics and related systems. We formulate the scattering problem for asymptotically flat, de Sitter, and anti-de Sitter spacetimes, and discuss the connections between transmission coefficients, absorption cross sections, Hawking radiation, and ringdown. We also review methods for their computation and survey recent developments, including the correspondence between grey-body factors and quasinormal modes, their stability under deformations of the effective potential, wormhole transmission and superradiance, and their behavior in modified theories of gravity. Finally, we discuss the appearance of grey-body factors in gauge/gravity duality, where absorption probabilities in the bulk are related to correlation functions and transport coefficients in the boundary theory.
item.dc:creator: Roman Konoplya, Alexander Zhidenko

item.title: Realistic neutron stars in the constant-Q branch of f(Q) gravity
item.description: arXiv:2610.36814v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the hydrostatic equilibrium and global structure of neutron stars within symmetric teleparallel gravity, where gravitational interactions are mediated by the non-metricity scalar $Q$. Working within the metric-affine formulation, we adopt the regular, constant-$Q$ branch ($Q = Q_*$) of $f(Q)$ gravity, which preserves regularity at the stellar centre while maintaining explicit dependence on the non-linear functional form through $f(Q_*)$ and its derivatives. We propose three novel non-linear $f(Q)$ extensions: (i) a Born-Infeld-inspired model, (ii) a Hu--Sawicki analogue, and (iii) a Tsujikawa-inspired model. Incorporating state-of-the-art realistic unified equations of state, namely GPPVA(DD2) and SLy4, we numerically solve the modified Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff equations and evaluate stellar stability via the Harrison-Zel'dovich-Novikov criterion. The Born-Infeld and Hu-Sawicki analogues smoothly recover the general relativistic limit as their control parameters increase, predicting stellar radii for low-mass objects ($M < 2.0\,M_\odot$) that match observational constraints from X-ray binaries and GW170817; however, their maximum masses remain capped below $2.43\,M_\odot$ (DD2) and $2.06\,M_\odot$ (SLy4). Conversely, the Tsujikawa-inspired model significantly stiffens the effective gravitational coupling, accommodating massive compact objects up to $\sim 3.36\,M_\odot$ and offering a viable physical origin for the $2.59_{-0.09}^{+0.08}\,M_\odot$ secondary object in GW190814, albeit at the expense of overpredicting radii for typical low-mass neutron stars. These contrasting behaviours demonstrate a key phenomenological complementarity between maximum mass and radius bounds within the constant-$Q$ framework, highlighting the utility of multimessenger observations in constraining non-linear non-metricity gravity.
item.dc:creator: Debadri Bhattacharjee, Pradip Kumar Chattopadhyay, P. H. R. S. Moraes

item.title: Rotation overcharges vectorized black holes
item.description: arXiv:2610.40179v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A charged black hole has a ceiling: extremality bounds the charge that a given mass and spin can support. Vector hair has so far only lowered it. In the Einstein--Maxwell--Vector (EMV) model, where a massless vector field couples nonminimally to the electromagnetic invariant, the spherically symmetric vectorized Reissner--Nordstr\"om black holes are strictly undercharged: vector hair is paid for in charge. Whether this ceiling is a property of the vector field or merely of spherical symmetry has remained open, because spherical symmetry hides the hair's mass as well: its Komar mass vanishes identically and the exact identity $M_V=2\Omega_HJ_V$ degenerates to $0=0$. Rotation lifts both degeneracies at once. We construct the rotating solutions of the model, the first in this setting, and find that the hair's mass is not a free parameter but a second-order invariant of the rotational response, fixed by $M_V=2\Omega_HJ_V$. Above a coupling threshold the ceiling gives way: the domain of existence crosses the extremal Kerr--Newman bound, reaching $q=Q/M>1$ with $q^2+\chi^2$ up to $1.84$, while at $\alpha=5$ the maximum charge stays below it. The shadow is where the hair becomes visible. At $(q,\chi)=(0.9947,0.10)$, near the extremal bound, the hair contributes an ellipticity of $8.30\%$, against $0.44\%$ from the charge and $0.06\%$ from rotation --- a factor of $19$ that charging a Kerr black hole cannot mimic; at the overcharged solution $(q,\chi)=(1.2527,0.10)$ the total ellipticity reaches $25.6\%$. Whether the branch is ghost-free remains open, but the existing no-go criteria do not settle it: they assume a background and a dispersion relation that do not hold here.
item.dc:creator: Shengjun Guo, Guangzai Ye, Peng Liu

item.title: Asymptotically Flat Rotating Topological Stars
item.description: arXiv:2510.05200v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We construct a new class of smooth, horizonless, non-supersymmetric solutions in five-dimensional minimal supergravity, which we call rotating topological stars. Built from a Kerr-Taub-bolt geometry embedded in five dimensions, they constitute the first rotating generalization of the topological star compatible with both smoothness in the interior and standard Kaluza-Klein asymptotics, S$^1\times\mathbb{R}^{1,3}$. The solutions carry angular momentum, magnetic and electric charges, and form a discrete tower of states labeled by a primary quantum number controlling the spin. Remarkably, despite lying outside the black-hole extremality bound, they can approach arbitrarily closely (in conserved charges) the Kerr black string with a large boost along the fifth dimension, making them relevant prototypes for rotating and astrophysical black-hole microstates. We analyze their geometry in detail, including their gravitational multipoles that can significantly deviate from those of black holes and the presence of an ergoregion, and show that both geodesics and scalar perturbations separate, paving the way for analyzing their dynamics in future work.
item.dc:creator: Pierre Heidmann, Paolo Pani, Jorge E. Santos

item.title: Decoherence and the Reemergence of Coherence From a Superconducting "Horizon"
item.description: arXiv:2603.16765v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In a recent paper [arXiv:2205.06279], Danielson et al. demonstrated that the mere presence of a black hole causes universal decoherence of quantum superpositions (dubbed the DSW decoherence). We analyze decoherence in a superconducting analogue [arXiv:1709.06154] of the event horizon of a late-stage black hole, where Andreev reflection plays the role of Hawking radiation. We consider a normal metal interferometer threaded by an Aharonov-Bohm flux, where one of the arms of the interferometer is coupled to a superconductor by a tunnel coupling of varying strength. At absolute zero temperature and for weak coupling, we find that the scattering states of the interferometer are decohered by Andreev reflection, a nontrivial manifestation of the proximity effect analogous to DSW decoherence from the event horizon of a black hole. However, for increasing coupling strength to the superconductor, we find a reemergence of coherence via resonant tunneling through Andreev bound states. This suggests the existence of an analogue gravitational phenomenon wherein transmission mediated by virtual Hawking radiation leads to a reemergence of coherence in an interferometer placed near a black hole's event horizon.
item.dc:creator: Eric J. Sung, Charles A. Stafford

item.title: Accretion-powered flares from black hole-disk collisions in galactic nuclei
item.description: arXiv:2604.07443v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Black hole impacts on accretion discs in galactic nuclei can power luminous transients, but predicting their observable signatures is challenging because the post-collision flow is highly time-dependent and inhomogeneous. We present a radiative post-processing framework for relativistic hydrodynamics simulations of black hole-disc collisions. Using physically motivated prescriptions for shock heating, optical depth via an eikonal solver, and photon escape fractions that account for photon trapping and diffusion, we predict light curves and spectral energy distributions over a range of disc densities and collision velocities. Our results indicate that the emission is dominated by the long-lived accretion flow onto the secondary black hole, whose mass supply is highly super-Eddington, rather than by cooling of the unbound ejecta. In the parameter range explored, the luminosity is typically of the order of the Eddington luminosity of the secondary and can reach several times this value, and the emission is generically dominated by soft X-rays. We find that lower velocity collisions produce brighter flares, while the disc surface density mainly controls spectral evolution: low-density discs typically produce $\sim$keV-peaked flares with weak spectral evolution, whereas high-density discs show softer early emission and late-time hardening. A depletion-time estimate calibrated to our results suggests characteristic durations of hours to days for intermediate-mass secondaries, and yields $t_{\rm flare} \propto P_{\rm QPE}$. We discuss implications for QPE-like transients and for the SMBH-binary candidate OJ 287. Our framework does not include radiative feedback on the gas, therefore the luminosities should be interpreted only as baseline estimates of the available power for radiation.
item.dc:creator: Joaquin Pelle, Kyohei Kawaguchi, Masaru Shibata, Alan Tsz-Lok Lam

item.title: Tachyonic Encore: A universal shift of inflationary observables
item.description: arXiv:2606.12549v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We propose a generic mechanism applicable to single-field inflaton models in which a light axion spectator, initialized near the hilltop of its potential, reshapes inflationary observables through purely gravitational multi-field dynamics. During inflation the axion is frozen and the background follows an effectively single-field trajectory. After inflation ends, the axion rolls, inducing a turn in field space and transient tachyonic phases of the isocurvature mode. The resulting ``tachyonic encore'' occurs entirely on super-horizon scales. These phases generate a nearly scale-invariant enhancement of the curvature power spectrum, suppressing the tensor-to-scalar ratio and shifting the scalar tilt to a weighted combination of adiabatic and entropic tilts at horizon crossing. We show that these effects can reconcile otherwise disfavored inflaton potentials with current CMB constraints. The same dynamics predict local non-Gaussianity, $f_{\rm NL}^{\rm loc.}\sim \mathcal{O}(1)$, within reach of upcoming surveys.
item.dc:creator: Diogo S. Gorgulho, Margherita Putti, Rodrigo Gonzalez Quaglia, Ema Dimastrogiovanni, Matteo Fasiello, Diederik Roest

item.title: Revisiting the Lyth bound constraints on inflation from ACT DR6 results
item.description: arXiv:2606.16711v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Lyth bound asserts that the field excursion of inflaton must be sub-Planckian, thereby imposing an upper bound on the amplitude of the tensor power spectrum in inflationary scenario. This bound is conventionally derived assuming a scale-invariant curvature power spectrum, i.e., $n_s = 1$. However, astrophysical observations confirm a red-tilted spectrum with $n_s < 1$. In light of recent results from the Atacama Cosmology Telescope (ACT) DR6, we revisit these constraints using the newly implied scalar spectral index of $n_s \simeq 0.9743$. Incorporating the ACT data yields a different upper bound on the tensor-to-scalar ratio $r$, which can potentially exclude inflationary scenarios previously robust under the original Lyth bound with $n_s = 1$. Our result highlights the urgent need to combine theoretical Lyth bound considerations with the most up-to-date astrophysical data.
item.dc:creator: Rui Yang, Jun Tao, Peng Wang, Mian Zhu
